id_and_class.theory_title: Malebranche’s Divine Occasionalism: Inner Sensation and Phenomenal Experience
id_and_class.summary: Nicolas Malebranche holds that sensations, emotions, pleasures, pains, and thoughts are real modifications of an immaterial soul, known immediately through inner sensation (sentiment intérieur). Bodies cannot cause these states: a brain event is only the occasion on which God, the sole true cause, produces the matching experience according to general laws of soul-body union. Ideas that represent bodies are not in us at all but in God, so what a perception represents comes apart from what it feels like.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Soul States Produced by God on Bodily Occasions

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Conscious states are modifications of an unextended thinking substance; consciousness itself is an inner sensation that attends every thought.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind and body never interact. Bodily changes are occasions on which God produces the corresponding mental states, and volitions are occasions on which God moves the body, all according to constant laws of the union of soul and body.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (sensations are modifications of an immaterial soul, produced directly by God rather than arising from matter)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Phenomenal states are directly present to the subject without inference. Intentional content comes from ideas in God, paradigmatically ‘intelligible extension’, while sensations themselves represent nothing.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Colors, sounds, tastes, warmth, pleasure, and pain belong to the soul, not to material objects. Built-in ‘natural judgments’ project them onto external things and body parts, for the organism’s guidance rather than to reveal what matter is.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Extended bodies with only geometrical and mechanical properties; finite immaterial souls; God as the only efficient cause; divine ideas, including intelligible extension; general psychophysical laws willed by God.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Inner sensation gives certainty that one thinks or feels but no clear idea of the soul’s nature. Malebranche argues that extension is more intelligible than the soul.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Three elements for every experience: the bodily event, the mental modification, and the divine action that links them. Perception combines intelligible structure from divine ideas with phenomenal modification in the soul.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (sensory qualities, pleasure, pain); Self-knowledge; Intentional representation; Voluntary action
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Occasionalism: God, acting by general rather than particular volitions, establishes brute psychophysical laws pairing brain states with experiences. Malebranche thus treats the correlation as law with no hidden mechanism beneath it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Phenomenal states exist in individual finite souls; ideas exist in or through the divine intellect.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Neither bodies nor finite minds have causal power, since a true cause must have a necessary connection to its effect and must know how to produce it. Sensation’s role is to guide an embodied creature toward what preserves it and away from harm.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: God maintains regular relations between bodily occasions and phenomenal responses, which makes the sensory world stable and coherent.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Ideas in God make spatial and geometrical features available to the intellect, while sensations supply the qualitative character. In his later doctrine of ‘efficacious ideas’, divine ideas take part in producing perceptions.
core_claims_and_evidence: No necessary connection can be discerned between any motion of nerve fibers and any sensation.
No finite mind knows how to produce a sensation of red in itself, so no finite mind produces one.
Sensible qualities are modifications of the soul and not properties of extended matter.
Inner sensation makes the existence of one’s thoughts certain while leaving the nature of the soul obscure.
Simple and constant laws express divine wisdom, so God acts by general volitions.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and theological: Cartesian metaphysics, analysis of causation, and arguments from divine omnipotence and wisdom.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Divine causation is neither measurable nor experimentally discriminable, so it cannot serve as a scientific mechanism. Saying God produces pain on the occasion of injury moves the question of causal efficacy without explaining why the state feels as it does. Arnauld attacked the doctrine of general volitions, holding that providence requires God to will every particular of creation.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The regularity of psychophysical laws depends wholly on a claim about divine nature; without the theology nothing in occasionalism forbids God from pairing different sensations with the same brain state each time.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent within Cartesian dualism plus theism, and it avoids the interaction problem by denying all created causation. Malebranche’s separation of representational content from phenomenal quality follows from a theological claim about where ideas are located.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since experiences are modifications of an immaterial soul produced by God, a machine’s states would at most be occasions, and nothing in the theory says God attaches a soul to them.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: The soul is an immaterial substance whose states are produced by God rather than by the body, so bodily death does not by itself end it.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: All causation is divine, and the mind’s union with God is more intimate than its union with its own body.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Copying bodily or neural patterns would copy only occasions, not the soul that undergoes experiences.
